title: Introduce workload fuzzing harness and dynamic golden-reference orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Our current benchmarking harness relies on a fixed set of canonical workloads and static golden baselines. This leaves gaps for rare attention patterns, adversarial sequence prefixes, and kernel-variant interactions that only appear in production traces. Goal: Build a workload fuzzing harness (stochastic workload generator + mutation strategies) that produces representative corner cases for prefill and decode scheduling, kernel-selection permutations, and attention memory shapes. Pair that harness with a dynamic golden-reference orchestration layer that can maintain multiple golden baselines per workload class and automatically select the appropriate baseline for CI, nightly runs, and canary experiments. Deliverables: 1) workload-fuzzer library (language-agnostic CLI + Python harness) that emits labelled workloads for length, sparsity, batched-prefix distributions, attention-window patterns, and KV-cache reuse scenarios; 2) orchestration metadata service (lightweight YAML manifest + selector rules) that maps workload families to golden baselines and acceptable deltas; 3) CI integration that runs selected fuzzed workloads in PR gates and nightly runners and records per-kernel and end-to-end token latency; 4) dashboards and alerting rules for regression detection and triage runbooks. Rationale and trade-offs: fuzzing increases test breadth but also CI cost; we will use sampled fuzz runs in PRs and full sweep in nightly pipelines. The orchestration layer favors reproducible baseline selection over on-the-fly golden creation to ensure auditability. Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Workload+Fuzzing+and+Golden+Orchestration, GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521, nightly dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/bench/workload-fuzzing, S3 artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/fuzzing-artifacts/2026-03
acceptance_criteria: Workload-fuzzer can generate 5 canonical workload families (short-chat, long-context prefix, KV-heavy, sparse-attention, hybrid-prefill) with seed-based reproducibility
Orchestration YAML format defined and validated; baseline selector returns a single baseline key for any workload in <500ms
CI PR gate runs a sampled fuzz subset within target additional latency <12 minutes and fails on >5% token-latency regression against selected golden baseline
Nightly full sweep produces per-kernel breakdown and stores artifacts to s3 path; dashboards show historical deltas and trigger regression alerts
Benchmark data ingestion includes kernel-tagging (kernel-name, quantization-profile) so downstream triage can attribute regressions
updates: 2026-02-08: RFC posted on Confluence outlining generator design and orchestration manifest. Requested feedback from ML infra and QA.

2026-02-14: Spike completed — implemented prototype fuzzer that mutates real production prefixes and emits length/attention masks. Initial results show previously-unseen kernel fallback on RNN->Attention transition (PR #4521).

2026-02-22: Design review with infra and SRE. Decision: sample fuzzing in PRs (10% of runs) and run full matrix nightly. Trade-off: PR latency vs flakiness risk; agreed to conservative thresholds for PR gates.
2026-03-02: Implemented orchestration YAML schema and selector service. Selector supports environment tags (hosted,dedicated,private) and hardware hints (A100,H100).

2026-03-09: Integration test failing intermittently for sparse-attention workloads on quantized kernels — assigned to eng kernel-owner for root-cause. Logged dependency ENG-17896 for trace-replay integration.
2026-03-12: PR review feedback addressed: added seed export, deterministic mutation mode, and improved CI runner containerization. Preparing canary on nightly pipeline next week.
Next: schedule canary run, finalize alert thresholds with SRE, and document triage playbook in runbook doc.
notes: Consider adding a lightweight cost-estimator to the orchestration so CI can smart-sample based on expected GPU-minutes.
Follow-up ticket suggested to add kernel microbenchmarks for mutated attention-window shapes (should be a separate ENG ticket).
